Definition: Whether the instant payment system enables or plans to enable instant payments across national borders to other countries or regional payment systems, supporting remittances, trade, and regional integration.
Comments: UNCDF report states cross-border interoperability is not established: “EBS, SRAG, and ECC do not have any connectivity outside Sudan’s borders,” indicating cross-border digital payment functionality is not available on national rails.
revision_notes: Fetched and read the cited UNCDF April 2023 report in full. It confirms the cited quote verbatim: 'Regarding cross-border interoperability, the EBS, SRAG, and ECC do not have any connectivity outside Sudan's borders.' The report further notes CBOS does not participate in the COMESA Regional Payment and Settlement System (REPSS) and that Sudan has only 'shown interest' in the Arab Monetary Fund's Buna platform. A follow-up search for later developments found an October 2025 statement by Sudan's Finance Minister expressing intent to join PAPSS/BRICS payment arrangements, but no evidence that Sudan is a live, connected member (PAPSS listed 16 member countries as of June 2025, not including Sudan). No operational cross-border functionality is confirmed. Score of 1 (No) confirmed.
revised_comments: Sudan's national payment rails - the Sudanese Real-time Automated Gross Settlement System (SRAG), the Electronic Banking Service Company (EBS) national switch, and the Electronic Cheque Clearing (ECC) system - have no connectivity outside Sudan's borders. The Central Bank of Sudan does not participate in the COMESA Regional Payment and Settlement System (REPSS), and Sudan is not yet a connected member of the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS), although the Ministry of Finance has expressed interest in joining PAPSS and in expanding local-currency trade arrangements. Cross-border instant payment functionality therefore remains unavailable.

Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: CBOS directly operates/owns key payment infrastructures: SRAG operating rules state “CBOS is the owner and operator of SRAG” with responsibility for day-to-day operations and oversight; UNCDF report also notes SRAG owned/operated by CBOS and CBOS licensing/oversight of mobile money operators integrated into EBS.
revision_notes: Fetched and read the UNCDF April 2023 report, which states plainly: 'The CBOS owns and operates the SRAG and has full responsibility and control of the day-to-day business operations of settlement accounts and operations,' and separately that CBOS licenses mobile money operators integrated into the EBS national switch. The originally cited CBOS SRAG Business Operating Rules PDF returned a 403 error on direct fetch, but its existence and CBOS authorship were independently confirmed via CBOS's own 'Regulations and Publications' index page (Arabic), which lists SRAG operating rules and procedures as CBOS-issued documents alongside the 2011 SRAG launch announcement. Evidence supports direct operation rather than mere regulatory oversight. Score of 5 (Direct Operation) confirmed.
revised_comments: The Central Bank of Sudan (CBOS) owns and directly operates the Sudanese Real-time Automated Gross Settlement System (SRAG), retaining full responsibility for its day-to-day settlement operations and oversight. CBOS also licenses and supervises the mobile money operators integrated into the national retail switch (EBS). This represents direct operational control of core payment infrastructure rather than an arm's-length regulatory role.

Definition: Whether national data protection or privacy legislation exists and explicitly covers payment transaction data, including provisions on data collection, storage, sharing, retention, and user rights over their payment data.
Comments: No comprehensive data protection law identified. Sources discussing Sudan’s privacy framework state Sudan lacks a dedicated data protection law/authority; existing protections are fragmented across sector laws (e.g., cybercrime/electronic transactions) and constitutional privacy provisions rather than general data protection legislation.
revision_notes: Fetched and read the cited 2019 Global Voices article, which confirms Sudan has no dedicated data protection law or authority, with only fragmented sectoral cybercrime/electronic transactions provisions in place. Ran follow-up searches for fresher evidence: Data Protection Africa's Sudan fact sheet and a November 2024 legal overview of Sudan's cybersecurity regulations both confirm the position is unchanged as of 2024 - no comprehensive data protection statute exists, a circa-2018 draft Data Protection Bill remains unenacted amid the ongoing conflict, and there is no independent data protection authority. No payment-specific data provisions were found. Score of 1 (No) confirmed with more current (2024) evidence.
revised_comments: Sudan has no comprehensive, general data protection or privacy statute. Personal data is protected only indirectly, through a constitutional privacy guarantee (Article 54 of the 2019 Constitutional Charter) and sectoral provisions in the Electronic Transactions Act 2007 and the Cybercrime (Informatic Offences) Act 2007 and its 2020 amendment. A draft Data Protection Bill dating to around 2018 has never been enacted, and no independent data protection authority exists. Payment transaction data is therefore not explicitly covered by dedicated privacy legislation.

Definition: Whether the scheme rules governing payment system participation, pricing structure, technical requirements, security standards, and conduct are publicly accessible via website, public repository, or on request. Transparency indicator.
Comments: Scheme/operating rules for SRAG are publicly downloadable from CBOS (e.g., “SRAG Business Operating Rules, 2011” and “SRAG Business Operating Procedures”).
revision_notes: The two originally cited CBOS PDF URLs (SRAG Business Operating Rules; SRAG Business Operating Procedures) returned a 403 error when fetched directly, likely a crawler block rather than a dead or unrelated link. Their existence and free public availability were independently confirmed via CBOS's own 'Regulations and Publications' (لوائح ومنشورات) index page, which lists 'قواعد تشغيل سراج' (SRAG operating rules) and 'اجراءات تشغيل سراج' (SRAG operating procedures) as downloadable CBOS documents alongside other payment-system directives (e.g. a 2013 policy on SRAG RSA security tokens). No registration or request process is indicated. Score of 3 (Yes - Fully Public) confirmed.
revised_comments: The operating rules and procedures governing Sudan's Real-time Automated Gross Settlement System (SRAG) are issued and published by the Central Bank of Sudan on its official regulations and publications page, alongside related payment-system directives. The documents are freely downloadable without registration or a request process, indicating full public transparency of scheme rules.
